$comment: The pipeline with the session interface reached from two places, as Flask 3.0.0 has it: the request context opens the session and process_response saves it. Calls land where the source makes them: the WSGI server calls wsgi_app, which pushes the context and calls full_dispatch_request; finalize_request calls process_response. The session is opened inside RequestContext.push, which the open_session relationship says rather than leaving the chain split. No views yet.

nodes.name: WSGI server
nodes.responsibility: Calls the application once per request

nodes.name: Flask.wsgi_app
nodes.responsibility: Pushes the request context and dispatches

nodes.name: Request context
nodes.responsibility: Binds request and session for one request and matches the URL

nodes.name: Session interface
nodes.responsibility: Opens and saves the signed cookie session

nodes.name: full_dispatch_request
nodes.responsibility: Preprocess, dispatch and finalize one request

nodes.name: dispatch_request
nodes.responsibility: Calls the view function of the matched rule

nodes.name: finalize_request
nodes.responsibility: Makes the response and runs process_response

nodes.name: View function
nodes.responsibility: The matched endpoint's function, in the application's own code

nodes.name: process_response
nodes.responsibility: Runs after_request functions and saves the session

edges.label: open_session
edges.description: RequestContext.push opens the session while it binds the request, so this call happens inside the push above
